headline: Singapore plants 1 million trees by 2030 to beat urban heat
meta_description: Singapore's ambitious tree-planting plan aims to reduce outdoor heat stress by up to 5°C through strategic shade placement in the city.
summary_short: Singapore is planting 1 million more trees by 2030. Research shows well-placed shade can cut outdoor heat stress by up to 5°C.
body:
Singapore is planting 1 million additional trees by 2030, backed by research showing that strategic shade dramatically reduces urban heat stress. Measurements taken across the city revealed that shaded locations provided significant relief compared to exposed areas.

The initiative tackles a growing problem in densely built environments: extreme outdoor temperatures that threaten public health and quality of life. By targeting tree placement based on scientific findings about shade effectiveness, Singapore is turning climate resilience into concrete action.

This approach moves beyond simple greening—it's designed around data showing exactly how much cooling shade delivers. The goal reflects a shift in urban planning where every tree planted serves a measurable purpose in making cities more livable as temperatures rise.
quick_facts: Shade can reduce outdoor heat stress by up to 5°C
City measurements confirm shaded spots provide significant cooling
